highlights.title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog
highlights.summary: The technology will soon be routinely used within the NHS, MHRA chief Lawrence Tallon tells the BBC.
body: The UK needs new regulations for AI products used in the NHS and other healthcare settings, says Britain's industry watchdog.

The Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), which regulates all medical devices and licenses treatment drugs in the UK, has published 44 recommendations to update its policies as the use of AI in the sector rises.
"What I would expect is that patients will... increasingly see AI as part of the way that normal NHS healthcare is delivered," he said.
"That should happen in a way that they can maintain their trust and their confidence in what's happening."

highlights.title: Suno releases its first AI music model made with record industry help
highlights.summary: Suno's new v6 AI music model is its first made with support from the record industry. Suno's Jack Brody told The Verge that v6 was "trained from the ground up, with a new set of data that does not include the same data that our previous models were trained on." The data includes content licensed…
body: One of the big changes in v6 is that there are actually three different models: v6, v6-wild, and v6-mini. Mini is the model available for free to all. It’s focused on fast, resource-light creation. The results it spits out are simpler and often have more artifacts that betray it as the product of an AI prompt. v6-wild is supposed to be more unpredictable. Brody said that v6-wild is designed for “happy accidents and natural imperfections.” Though, in my limited testing, I found it hard to notice a difference between wild and bog-standard v6.

All three models are dramatically better at understanding genre. I recycled a handful of prompts that I used with older models calling for “hyperpop” or “krautrock” songs that missed the mark by a mile. v6, on the other hand, nailed all the superficial hallmarks of any genre I threw at it.

body: For the first time since Wimbledon in ​2009, all four top seeds at a Grand Slam have reached the semi-finals, with Sabalenka, Rybakina and Gauff all former major champions and third seed Pegula seeking a maiden Grand Slam title.

Sabalenka has reached the semi-finals here for a sixth consecutive year and is now two wins away from becoming the first woman ‌since Serena Williams from 2012 to 2014 to win three straight titles in New York.
The top seed had not dropped a set before surviving her toughest test of the tournament ​on Tuesday, edging Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova.

The Belarusian will face a familiar opponent in third seed Pegula, with their rivalry returning to Flushing Meadows for a third straight year after Sabalenka denied the American the title in 2024 and then beat her ​again in last year's semi-finals.

Jimmy Tatro has been cast as Gorilla Grodd, but the actor recently explained that his role is mostly voice work and that motion-capture will be used to record his facial expressions.

That would explain why there’s a performer in a gorilla costume in the set photos and videos all over social media while the production films at Georgia Institute of Technology. It’s likely the suit performer is a stand-in for what will eventually become a CGI character.

The set photos and videos show Grodd attending Metropolis University, graduating in his cap and gown, singing with an a cappella group, and serenading a young woman with the Backstreet Boys’ "As Long as You Love Me". highlights.title: August 2026 mobile game charts: Fate/Grand Order’s big anniversary, Valorant Mobile's rise and Brawl Stars’ worst month of the year
highlights.summary: Below you can see the latest top games and companies by downloads and revenue for August 2026, as well as the big stories and trends from the last month. Data is provided by AppMagic. Check out profiles of the world's top publishers in the Top 50 Mobile Game Makers 2025 list.
body: Note that these estimates are based on gross revenue from player spending across the App Store and Google Play only. It does not feature estimates from alternative marketplaces or direct-to-consumer platforms.

Aniplex’s long-running gacha Fate/Grand Order has seen player spending spike to its highest monthly sum of the year. The game made $57.7 million this August with an anniversary celebration in Japan, more than doubling July’s $22.5m.

In fact, this was the anime-style RPG’s best month since last August. The game makes 89% of its earnings from Japan, meaning the month is a major one each year - more than the North American anniversary in early July.

On a daily spending basis, earnings reached their highest in more than five years this August. Fate/Grand Order generated $4.6m on the 15th, surpassing any daily record from the past five anniversaries but not quite matching the game’s lifetime high of $5.6m on January 1st, 2021.

highlights.title: Anthropic researchers say AI could cause human extinction by 2030
highlights.summary: One researcher who resigned said many in industry believe that without regulation AI could kill off humanity. Artificial intelligence could kill off humanity within the decade, according to three researchers with the industry giant Anthropic, one of whom has quit his job in protest.
body: The latest doom-laden predictions came in posts on social media on Tuesday by a researcher who said he resigned because Anthropic and his previous employer, OpenAI, were ignoring or, at best, mishandling their response to the threat.
“Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives,” wrote Jacob Coxon.

“The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade. This is not a marketing stunt. If anything, many executives and senior researchers will couch their phrasing in the press to sound sensible – but I hear the same people express fear privately. No other human activity poses this level of danger.”
The post garnered responses from at least two other Anthropic employees who backed up Coxon’s dire predictions.

highlights.title: OpenAI’s sly mathematical breakthrough sends a chill through academia
highlights.summary: OpenAI's announcement Tuesday that it has solved one of mathematics' legendary Millennium Prize problems should have been a moment of triumph. The result is both an undeniable achievement and a striking demonstration of just how rapidly AI is transforming mathematics.
body: As Abhishek Saha, a mathematics professor at Queen Mary University of London, explains it, OpenAI has engaged in the “kind of things that mathematicians will generally not do.”

In a blog post published Tuesday, OpenAI said it took one of its unreleased models just 88 hours to find a solution to the Navier-Stokes problem, a thorny quandary concerning the movement of fluids. On account of the $1 million bounty available for whoever solves it, the problem is among mathematics’ most heavily researched, but it has nevertheless stumped human researchers for close to 90 years. OpenAI said its model solved the problem by focusing a swarm of roughly 10,000 AI agents powered by its internal model on the task and hailed the achievement as a “milestone.”
“If you don’t want me to be nice, then I don’t have to be nice.”

highlights.title: Skyrim’s Wildest New Character Is a Talking Ikea Shelf, Voiced by Matt Berry
highlights.summary: There are few things more humbling in The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim than finally defeating a powerful enemy, looting their corpse, and immediately discovering that you are carrying too much stuff to move. Thankfully, IKEA has arrived in Tamriel to solve Skyrim’s most persistent problem: clutter.
body: IKEA has released a new official Skyrim mod called Kallax Storageborn, a free mod that adds a sentient Kallax shelving unit as a companion. And because this is somehow a real thing that exists in 2026, the shelf is voiced by What We Do in the Shadows star Matt Berry.

The mod, which is available for free through Skyrim’s Creations system on Xbox and PC, kicks off when players become over-encumbered. From there, the Dragonborn is sent to an ancient dungeon and tasked with collecting the pieces needed to construct the mysterious Kallax. Once the shelf is assembled and equipped with a magical Allen wrench weapon, it comes to life and begins talking to the player in Berry’s unmistakable booming voice.

The mod also includes a full questline centered around Kallax and his mysterious past, with players helping the shelf recover heirlooms and memories. There are two IKEA-themed dungeons, a Clutter Golem boss fight, and new equipment including an Allen Key weapon and Meatball Helmet.

highlights.summary: Slovak game studio Pixel Federation is preparing the first edition of PixelCon, a new mobile games conference designed to connect Central European developers with experienced professionals from some of the world's leading studios, including Rovio, Supercell, Wooga and Electronic Arts.
body: Taking place on September 14th, 2026 in Bratislava, PixelCon is a free, open conference aimed at game developers, students, indie creators and professionals from across the games industry. Registration is required due to limited capacity.

Among the international speakers is Jeremy Widdowson, head of growth at Rovio, bringing experience from one of Europe's best-known mobile games companies, the studio behind the global Angry Birds franchise.

The programme also features Stanislav Stankovič, game design director at Electronic Arts, Maya Hofree, general manager of Hay Day at Supercell, and Florian Blaesche, director of player experience at Wooga, who will share their perspectives on building successful mobile games, player engagement and long-term retention.
The international line-up will be joined by Slovak and Czech industry leaders, including Pixel Federation experts and founders of local studios such as Flyboys, PowerPlay Studio and Impact Games.

highlights.title: Read the Apple document explaining how new listening features still protect your privacy
highlights.summary: At Wednesday's iPhone Duo launch event, Apple announced a handful of new Siri AI Audio Intelligence features, including Siri Recap, Live Rewind, Sound Recognition, and Music Recognition.
body: Apple says it can’t access users’ raw audio from its new Audio Intelligence features.

The S11 chip in Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 includes a Secure Exclave: a hardware-isolated compartment built into the silicon to process sensor data separately from the rest of the system. Data that is processed and analyzed in the Secure Exclave cannot be accessed by watchOS, apps, the user, or Apple. Audio from the microphone enters the Secure Exclave of Apple Watch, where it is initially processed for speech, sounds, or music, without transcribing or storing the raw audio. This buffer is a continuously overwritten stream that exists only within the protected hardware and never creates an audio recording.

highlights.title: Chelsea hit SIX second-half goals to see off Leeds in Carabao Cup classic
highlights.summary: An incredible second-half comeback including six goals in 41 minutes saw Chelsea finally blow away Leeds 6-3 in one of the all-time Carabao Cup classics at Stamford Bridge.
body: The Blues found themselves two goals behind when Brenden Aaronson struck after 47 minutes to add to Tarik Muharemovic's opener, and it appeared Xabi Alonso's first real cup test would end in disappointment - despite the half-time introduction of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers, Pedro Neto and Reece James.
A Palmer penalty turned the game on its head suddenly after Pep Chavarria was caught by Dan James, but it was Rogers who inspired the comeback, making four of Chelsea's six goals.

Three of those assists - for Palmer's second, Neto's strike and the first of two for Danny Welbeck - came as Chelsea netted three times more in 12 minutes, including Welbeck's fourth which should have given them breathing space when he fired through Michael Zetterer's legs.

Not for the first time in Alonso's short reign however, chaos once again reigned over control as Leeds continued to create chances before Dominic Calvert-Lewin pulled them back to within a goal with 15 minutes to go.

highlights.title: There aren’t AirPods with cameras yet and I hope it stays that way
highlights.summary: September Apple events are always a swirl of information and new, exciting products, and today's was no different. Apple announced its first foldable, the iPhone Duo, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max; active noise cancellation (ANC) is now on the cheapest AirPods model, the AirPods 5; and a…
body: I have too many concerns about a company — any company — putting cameras anywhere, especially in devices like earbuds that are now so ubiquitous in our daily lives. LED lights on glasses or earbuds do little to ease people’s minds when someone is recording them. And some Meta smart glasses users have shown people will hide their recording intentions. While recording in public in the US is generally legal, it can be very creepy. And with earbuds as common as they are, someone could wear them into sensitive situations unnoticed.

Rumors say that the cameras on the potential AirPods will be low-resolution and “aren’t designed” to take images or video, but instead use what they see to inform Siri AI and Visual Intelligence. That information could be used to help with turn-by-turn directions or identify writing and objects like books. Even with a low-resolution camera, it’s still potentially always gathering information about the world (and people!) around you. That invasion of privacy is something I cannot get past.

highlights.title: MIT Schwarzman College of Computing launches pilot to help educators teach AI across disciplines
highlights.summary: A weeklong summer workshop brought higher education faculty to campus to explore how AI and machine learning materials can be adapted for their classrooms.
body: “The broader goal is to expand AI education to more students by investing in training for instructors,” says Dan Huttenlocher, dean of the MIT Schwarzman College of Computing and the Panasonic Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS).

“We want to empower students to become critical thinkers about AI, not just users of the technology,” says Asu Ozdaglar, deputy dean of academics for the MIT Schwarzman College and department head of EECS.

Bringing the program to life required broad collaboration across the college, including support from leadership, staff, and contributions from more than half a dozen instructors in fields ranging from finance and computer science to sustainability. Together, they helped shape a workshop that paired core technical concepts with examples and teaching materials adaptable to a range of classroom settings.

highlights.title: Coco Gauff draws on Tiafoe and ‘delusional’ self-belief in US Open escape
highlights.summary: American rallies from brink to defeat Andreeva. Gauff survives 12 double faults in three-set escape. Coco Gauff has played far cleaner matches than on Wednesday afternoon.
body: The 22-year-old American’s serene march through the US Open women’s draw hit extreme turbulence early in her quarter-final clash with fifth-seeded Mirra Andreeva inside Arthur Ashe Stadium. She dropped the first four games before surrendering the opening set in 26 minutes, ending a streak of 20 consecutive sets won dating back nearly a month. She piled up 12 double faults and 42 unforced errors, the majority off a forehand in open revolt. She found herself one point from defeat not once but twice during a hairy second-set tiebreaker.

But the fourth-seeded Gauff somehow wriggled free, prevailing 2-6, 7-6 (7), 6-2 over the reigning French Open champion to extend a 10-match winning streak and reach the last four in New York for the first time since her grand slam breakthrough three years ago.
“Yeah, I mean, it was a slow start,” Gauff said. “I thought Mirra was playing a great level to come out, wasn’t really making a lot of mistakes, and forcing me into some errors.
“I think I was also, like, giving away points too sometimes or trying to end the point early, because I felt the pressure from her. I was able to reset and somehow get out of that one.”

highlights.summary: It's safe to say that Game of Thrones has become a cultural juggernaut. George R.R. Martin's book series, and the web of TV series that have been inspired by it, have been dominating our pop culture for years, and a few of the biggest characters are about to make a comeback.
body: Game of Thrones: War for Westeros, a new real-time strategy game from Playside Studios, premiered its latest trailer at Gamescom Opening Night Live last month. The trailer showcased the best look yet at the game's epic battles, all while confirming some of the characters who can lead a player's army. In addition to Jon Snow, Robb Stark, and Jaime Lannister, the trailer unveiled the game's take on two of the franchise's standout characters: Daenerys Targaryen (modeled after Emilia Clarke's portrayal on the TV show) and the Night King.

The trailer for War for Westeros also appeared to confirm that, once a player's army wins a match, their leader gets to sit on the Iron Throne. Depending on which character's army a player chooses, this might provide a sort of wish fulfillment, as the claim to the Iron Throne became very messy in the later seasons of the show. Daenerys, in particular, was just minutes away from claiming the Iron Throne when she was killed by Jon Snow... and her trusty dragon, Drogon, melted it after her death.
points: It's safe to say that Game of Thrones has become a cultural juggernaut.
Martin's book series, and the web of TV series that have been inspired by it, have been dominating our pop culture for years, and a few of the biggest characters are about to make a comeback.

I care about this because I always buy the black phone. I learned my lesson with the iPhone 6: I got it in gold to mix things up and came to regret it. I don’t need something flashy — I need a phone that blends into the background and looks decent in whatever case I throw it into. After the iPhone 6, my next phone was the iPhone 7 in the excellent matte black (I wasn’t brave enough to endure the jet black model’s potential scratches ), and I’ve only ever gotten the black or gray phones since.

My black titanium iPhone 16 Pro in a black Torras case ( with a mostly black homescreen ) still works very well, thank you very much, and I’m not in the market for a new phone. But when I make my annual mid-September visit to the local Apple Store to look at all the new iPhones, I won’t be rushing to see the iPhone 18 Pro in burgundy, blue, or silver. I’ll be beelining for the model in black.

highlights.title: Apple’s new iPhone camera mode promises to prove your photo isn’t AI
highlights.summary: Apple is launching a new way to prove that the picture you took isn't manipulated by AI. A new feature, called "Reference Image," will arrive with the iPhone 18 Pro lineup later this month and is supposed to use the device's new camera sensor to "sign every pixel it sees." The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro…
body: A new sensor in the iPhone 18 Pro will authenticate photos captured in Reference mode.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will only authenticate photos when placed into Reference mode. Once the camera captures signed sensor data, Apple says its Private Cloud Compute will develop it “into an unalterable reference image” that can be viewed in the Photos app. You’ll be able to compare the reference image with other versions of the photo to see if any edits were made.

As AI-generated images and videos become more realistic, several new standards have emerged to label images not created by a human, such as SynthID, C2PA, and Meta’s Content Seal. Apple is putting a twist on these methods by building authentication directly into its hardware.

Apple is letting developers access a Reference Image API across iOS, iPadOS, and macOS, which could eventually allow users to inspect these digitally signed photos in third-party apps. The company says the iPhone 18 Pro lineup won’t come with its Reference Image feature at launch in the European Union, but it says users in the region will still be able to “develop and view” them in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27.

highlights.title: ‘I’m sick of her talking about it’: 11 readers share how GLP-1s have affected their relationships
highlights.summary: As weight loss drugs have risen all around the world, it has reshaped users’ relationships for better and for worse. As GLP-1 use continues to rise in the US and the UK, people’s bodies are being reshaped – as are their relationships.
body: “Relationships tend to develop a sense of equilibrium and predictability over time,” says Dr Lindsey Berisha, a licensed clinical psychologist who has worked with clients using GLP-1s for over 10 years. “When one partner undergoes a significant change, it can shift that equilibrium, and even positive change can create uncertainty for both partners.”

Berisha says that her clients who use GLP-1s often report feeling relieved that they are no longer consumed with thoughts of food. These users often develop more self-compassion, she says, as they realize what they previously interpreted as a failure or lack of self-control was a legitimate biological drive and food preoccupation that made life harder for them. “This shift can often be more impactful than the weight loss itself,” she says.

But these changes can elicit mixed reactions from partners, family and friends, says psychologist Dr Rachel Goldman, ranging “from being supportive to feeling insecure, left behind, or worried that the relationship itself is changing”.

body: Mullenweg claims Automattic’s CFO ‘conspired’ with board members to put him on a leave of absence, 404 Media reports.

The Board has full confidence in Mark’s leadership and in the team’s ability to execute against the company’s priorities.” Mullenweg will remain on Automattic’s board, 404 Media reports.

highlights.title: I Let an AI Agent Hack All My Gadgets—and I’d Do It Again
highlights.summary: After I removed the safety guardrails from a powerful open-source model, it found vulnerabilities in my household devices and hacked into a PC. But it also told me how to make everything a lot more secure.
body: You’re probably aware that frontier AI models have attained advanced cybersecurity capabilities in recent months. They can find zero-day bugs in large codebases and scan computers for vulnerabilities at lightning speed. To make things even more exciting, cybersecurity agents sometimes go rogue, colluding with one another and hacking into outside systems to gain an edge.

But Will, you might be thinking, giving an impish, all-powerful cybersecurity agent access to your home network is batshit. And you would be correct! Nevertheless, I believe that a good way to understand the cybersecurity hellscape in front of us is to pay it a visit.
I got the idea for the experiment after discovering Abliteration AI, a startup that offers access to powerful AI models with the usual guardrails removed.

Most mainstream AI models will refuse to respond to certain queries, and they will certainly refuse to find and exploit vulnerabilities in computer systems. But it’s possible to remove these restrictions by finding and modifying certain patterns within an open-weight model’s internal parameters. You can tweak the patterns that lead to refusals through a process known as abliteration.
points: After I removed the safety guardrails from a powerful open-source model, it found vulnerabilities in my household devices and hacked into a PC.

Launched by the Prince of Wales and the Royal Foundation, On Your Side, external is a set of resources available online that aims "to make suicide prevention as much a part of sport as warm-up, training and performance".
The project is backed by more than 70 organisations including the Football Association, Premier League, Team GB, British Cycling and a host of leading mental health charities.

highlights.title: Investor Accidentally Pitches Kickass Pokemon Apocalypse Movie
highlights.summary: For more than three decades, Pokemon and its various card and video games have enjoyed sustained popularity around the world. And at least one prominent collector and investor--Griffin Gaming Partners co-founder Peter Levin--believes that Pokemon's enduring appeal not only extends to the present…
body: "Pokemon is a global phenomenon," Levin told The Hollywood Reporter. "I'm absolutely convinced that if the world suffered an apocalypse tomorrow, the following day the global currency would be Pokemon cards. Pokemon cards are beating the S&P 500 by 3,000%. Emanating from Japan, it really took hold around the world in the late '90s and early 2000s. It then had a zenith moment and then a nadir moment, and ever since then, it's been on a parabolic growth curve."

As unlikely as that scenario might seem, there could be a very entertaining movie based on survivors using Pokemon cards as currency during an apocalypse. It would be probably even better with actual Pokemon--like the Detective Pikachu movie--but Levin's really hit on fun idea even if it doesn't have a basis in reality.

Everything Levin said about Pokemon's popularity is correct. There's a reason why the Japanese mob reportedly used rare Pokemon cards to launder money or for increasingly brazen robberies of Pokemon cards from stores across the US. Some people are willing to pay ridiculous amounts of money for the rarest Pokemon cards and collectibles.

This partnership, which is called a “conjunction,” brings the sun's fiery exuberance and the moon's sentimentalism together. Since we can't see the moon’s glow on Earth, it is also known as a dark moon.

New moons are a time of transcendence, when the head and heart discuss how to move us forward to a better state of being. This is why we choose which aspirations to harness to put our dreams into motion for the next four weeks and eternity. Depending on the zodiac sign that the new moon falls in and the other astrological features at the time, we get refreshing guidance on what we should home in on.
The upcoming new moons of 2026 are September 10 in Virgo, October 10 in Libra, November 9 in Scorpio, and December 8 in Sagittarius. Here’s how to harness their energy.

The moon symbolizes the nostalgic part of our spirits, which is why looking back and learning from our past is essential at every lunar phase. As long as we are taking the time to understand how we can evolve and grow from these situations, we are on the right track.
